title: Sing Buri & Chai Nat 2-Day Trip: Dam, Bird Park & Riverside Food | ThailandAddict
metaDesc: A 2-day, 1-night Sing Buri to Chai Nat road trip in Thailand. Day 1: Bang Rachan history, the Reclining Buddha, and Mae La snakehead fish. Day 2: Chao Phraya Dam, Chai Nat Bird Park, and Luang Pu Sukh's temple — with real times, fees, and where to eat.
keywords: Sing Buri Chai Nat trip, Chao Phraya Dam, Chai Nat Bird Park, Thailand road trip, Bang Rachan
h1:
Sing Buri & Chai Nat in 2 Days
Dam, Bird Park, and Riverside Eats
intro: Sing Buri and Chai Nat sit side by side along Thailand's Asia Highway, and it's only about a 40-minute drive between the two towns — so it's easy to pair them in one trip. Day one is a history walk through Bang Rachan plus a visit to Sing Buri's giant Reclining Buddha, lunch on Mae La snakehead fish by the river, and one night's stay. Day two you cross into Chai Nat to see the Chao Phraya Dam up close, walk through the bird park with its huge open aviary, then pay respects at Luang Pu Sukh's temple before heading home. Here's the plan with real timings and where to actually eat.

blocks.html: This trip works best if you're driving yourself, because the sights are spread out along both banks of the Chao Phraya in each province and public transport between them is thin. From Bangkok, take the Asia Highway (Route 32) north — it's about 2 hours to Sing Buri town. From there, Chai Nat town is roughly another 40 minutes further north. You can base your overnight stay in either Sing Buri or Chai Nat, depending on which side you'd rather wake up on.

items: Day 1 — Sing Buri: Bang Rachan Heroes Monument → Wat Pho Kao Ton → Wat Phra Non Chaksi → Mae La snakehead fish by the river → check in
Day 2 — Chai Nat: Chao Phraya Dam → Chai Nat Bird Park → Wat Pak Khlong Makham Thao (Luang Pu Sukh) → boat noodles before heading home
Total distance: everything sits within a fairly short radius, with each stop about a 10–30 minute drive apart — ideal for an easy trip with no need to rush

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Sing Buri — the Bang Rachan trail and the Reclining Buddha

items.activity: Arrive at the Bang Rachan Heroes Monument, Khai Bang Rachan district
items.note: The monument casts the 11 village leaders in bronze, set in a shady park, with the Bang Rachan Heroes Museum next to it telling the story of their roughly five-month stand against the Burmese army. Free entry, and an easy spot to walk around and take photos.

items.activity: Stop at Wat Pho Kao Ton nearby
items.note: This temple is believed to be the site of the Bang Rachan camp, with old bodhi trees and a quiet atmosphere. It doesn't take long to look around.

items.activity: Drive into town and visit Wat Phra Non Chaksi Worawihan
items.note: A large stucco Reclining Buddha, over 47 meters long, and one of Sing Buri's oldest and most revered. It's about 4 km out of town along the Sing Buri–Suphan Buri road, and open daily.

items.activity: Lunch on Mae La snakehead fish by the river
items.note: Well-known spots here include Mae La Pla Phao (along the Asia Highway in Bang Man) for grilled Mae La snakehead and chu chi sheatfish, or Baan Suan Mae La Karong, which sits right on the Mae La stream. The firm-fleshed snakehead fish is the province's signature dish.

items.activity: Wander the old market or a riverside cafe in town
items.note: Settle your stomach with Thai sweets or coffee. By mid-afternoon the sun has softened, so it's a comfortable time to stroll along the Chao Phraya.

items.activity: Check in at your hotel in Sing Buri town
items.note: There are hotels in town across a range of price points. Rest up so you can start early and cross over to Chai Nat the next morning.

blocks.title: A note on timing
blocks.html: Many of the Mae La snakehead and boat noodle places close in the afternoon to early evening rather than staying open late. Plan lunch and dinner before nightfall to be safe — don't count on eating at 8 p.m.

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Chai Nat — Chao Phraya Dam, the bird park, and Luang Pu Sukh

items.activity: Leave Sing Buri and drive north into Chai Nat
items.note: It takes about 40 minutes to reach the Chao Phraya Dam area in Sapphaya district. Setting off a little early gives you nicer light and beats the heat.

A large water-regulating dam on the Chao Phraya River and a landmark Chai Nat has been known for over many decades. Walk along the dam crest and photograph the wide river views — it's especially nice during and just after the rainy season when the water is brimming.

Open roughly 08:00–18:00, with adult entry in the low tens of THB and cheaper for kids. The highlight is the huge open aviary where the birds live together close to nature, plus a hall showcasing Chao Phraya basin fish and a man-made waterfall. It's an easy walk for the whole family — set aside about 1.5–2 hours.

items.activity: Lunch in Chai Nat town or by the river
items.note: Pick a riverside spot for Chao Phraya river fish, or a made-to-order place in town. Take a break before the afternoon leg.

items.activity: Wat Pak Khlong Makham Thao (Luang Pu Sukh's temple)
items.note: An old riverside temple about 25 km out of Chai Nat town, where followers of the revered monk Luang Pu Sukh come to pray for blessings. Inside you can see murals painted by Prince Chumphon and Luang Pu Sukh's old kuti (monk's quarters).

items.activity: Boat noodles or souvenirs before heading home
items.note: Wrap up with a bowl of rich, local-style boat noodles before getting back on the Asia Highway to Bangkok — about 2.5–3 hours.

blocks.text: What stands out at each place, in brief

items.name: Chao Phraya Dam
items.blurb: A big water-regulating dam and a Chai Nat landmark. Wide river views, free to walk the dam crest for photos — good for a morning stop.

items.name: Chai Nat Bird Park
items.blurb: A large open aviary, plus a freshwater fish hall and a man-made waterfall. Entry in the low tens of THB, and an easy walk for the whole family.

items.name: Bang Rachan Camp
items.blurb: Monument to the 11 village heroes, with a museum telling the story of villagers fighting the Burmese army. Free entry.

items.name: Wat Phra Non Chaksi
items.blurb: A stucco Reclining Buddha over 47 meters long, old and revered, about 4 km outside town.

blocks.text: Food you shouldn't skip along this route

items.name: Grilled Mae La snakehead fish
items.blurb: Sing Buri's signature dish — snakehead from the Mae La stream, firm and sweet, grilled in salt and eaten with nam jim jaew. Order it alongside pla luy suan. Well-known spots include Mae La Pla Phao and Baan Suan Mae La Karong.

items.name: Boat noodles
items.blurb: Noodles in a rich, boldly seasoned broth — an Asia Highway staple that's easy to find around Sing Buri and Chai Nat. Most shops open from morning into the afternoon.
items.meta: Breakfast–lunch · from low tens of THB a bowl

items.name: Chao Phraya river fish
items.blurb: Riverside restaurants in both provinces serve fresh freshwater fish — sheatfish, featherback and more — done many ways. Great for a big family meal.

blocks.title: The best time to visit
blocks.html: The riverside in both provinces is at its best from late rainy season into early winter (around October to January), when the air cools, the dam is full, and walking outdoors is comfortable. In the April hot season the sun is fierce, so visit outdoor spots in the morning or evening.

One night is just right for this trip. Staying in Sing Buri town puts you roughly in the middle of the route, so you can do the Sing Buri sights on day one and cross to Chai Nat early on day two without any hassle. If you'd rather hit the dam and bird park first thing without rushing, basing yourself on the Chai Nat side works just as well. See the accommodation options in the guide below.

faq.q: How far apart are Sing Buri and Chai Nat by car?
faq.a: From Sing Buri town to Chai Nat town it's about a 40-minute drive north on the Asia Highway (Route 32). The riverside sights in both provinces sit within a fairly short radius, so it's easy to pair them in one trip.

faq.q: How much is Chai Nat Bird Park, and what are the hours?
faq.a: Chai Nat Bird Park is open roughly 08:00–18:00 daily, with adult entry in the low tens of THB and cheaper for kids. The highlights are the huge open aviary and the hall showcasing Chao Phraya basin fish. Set aside about 1.5–2 hours to walk it.

faq.q: Do you need your own car for this trip?
faq.a: Driving yourself is recommended, since the sights are spread out along the rivers in both provinces and public transport between them is thin. If you don't have a car, renting one or hiring a car with driver is the most convenient option.

faq.q: When is the best time to visit Sing Buri and Chai Nat?
faq.a: Late rainy season into early winter, around October to January, when the weather is cool and the Chao Phraya Dam is full and looking its best. You can walk the dam and the bird park outdoors without it being too hot.

faq.q: What food should you try along this route?
faq.a: Grilled Mae La snakehead fish is Sing Buri's signature dish, followed by rich boat noodles and Chao Phraya river fish dishes at the riverside restaurants in both provinces.
